Title: Exposure to light and other radiation
Description: Exposure to light and other radiation applies to cases in which the injury or illness resulted from exposure to any type of radiation either ionizing or non-ionizing. Exposure to light (code 5211) includes exposures from various types of light: ultraviolet and visible, laser light, infrared light, sunlight, and welding flash. Included in this code are flash burns from viewing ultraviolet (UV) light, sunburn and sun poisoning, and eye injuries from laser beams or electrical sparks. Exposure to other radiation (code 5212) includes exposures to microwaves and radio waves, radars, and other power frequencies. Radiant heat burns are classified in 533, Contact with hot objects or substances, and sunstroke and other heat-related incidents are classified in 531, Exposure to environmental heat.

Description: Incidents where a skier falls to the same or lower level in any location and is not the result of a collision or being struck by a non-transport object.

Title: Ski, snowboard, and sled incidents— n.e.c.
Description: Incidents occurring while skiing that are known but do not fit descriptions of events 2431 through 2433.

Title: Vehicle struck by falling or flying object(s) in roadway
Description: Moving vehicles that are struck by falling or collapsing objects in the roadway.
Notes: Falling tree/landslide is one inclusion among many

Title: Vehicle struck by falling or flying object(s), nonroadway
Description: Moving vehicles or mobile equipment that are struck by falling or collapsing objects in nonroadway or private roadway areas.
Notes: Falling tree/landslide is one inclusion among many

Title: Forest fire or wildfire
Description: Large scale fires that spread over woodland or brush. They may burn over long durations of several days to several weeks. Forest fires or wildfires causing a structure or other object to catch fire are coded here.

Title: Direct exposure to electricity— greater than 220 volts
Description: This code classifies cases resulting in electrical injuries due to direct contact between the power source and the person when the voltage is greater than 220 volts
Notes: Lightning is one inclusion among others

Title: Indirect exposure to electricity— greater than 220 volts
Description: This code classifies cases resulting in injuries due to indirect electrical contact between the power source and the person when the voltage is greater than 220 volts
Notes: Lightning is one inclusion among others

Title: Exposure to light, other radiation— single episode or single shift
Description: This code classifies injuries that are the result of exposure to light and other types of radiation from a single episode or in a single shift.
Notes: Sunburn/sun exposure is one inclusion among others

Title: Exposure to environmental heat
Description: This code classifies injuries and illnesses resulting from ambient heat and high temperatures in the workplace where direct contact with a heated object did not occur. Cases where heat was deemed to have played a role in exacerbating an underlying medical condition or provoking a reaction to medication should still be coded here, unless the reaction was due to non-medical use of drugs (551).

Title: Exposure to environmental heat— unspecified
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to environmental heat— indoor
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to environmental heat— outdoor
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to environmental cold
Description: This code classifies injuries and illnesses resulting from cold temperatures in the workplace where direct contact with a cold object did not occur.

Title: Exposure to environmental cold— unspecified
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to environmental cold— indoor
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to environmental cold— outdoor
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to air and water pressure change
Description: Codes in this major group apply to injuries that are the result of bodily reaction to changes in air and water pressure.

Title: Exposure to air and water pressure change— unspecified
Description: This code classifies injuries from bodily reactions to changes in pressure when it is unknown whether air pressure or water pressure was responsible.

Title: Exposure to change in water pressure
Description: This code classifies injuries from bodily reactions to changes in water pressure.

Title: Exposure to change in air pressure
Description: This code classifies injuries from bodily reactions to changes in air pressure.

Title: Drowning, submersion without other event
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Exposure to stressful environment without other event
Description: This code applies to events where the worker is affected by stressful events on the job with the exception of being a victim or witness of violent act(s) or threatening actions provoking a reasonable fear of violence. Stress from being involved in another event such as a transportation incident or fire should be coded to that event. Assume events and actions of persons are unintentional unless source documents support clear intent to harm oneself or another person.
Notes: Stressful environment; review definition

Title: Exposure to stressful environment without other event— duration unspecified
Description: Exposure to workplace stress of unknown duration

Title: Exposure to stressful environment— prolonged
Description: Exposure to a workplace stressor for longer than one shift

Title: Exposure to stressful environment— single episode
Description: Stress resulting from witnessing a single traumatic, non violent work event where the worker was not the direct victim of the incident.

Title: Collapse, engulfment— loose materials or liquids
Description: Partial or total engulfment in loose materials or liquids. May involve sinking into materials or being overtaken by collapsing or surging materials
Notes: Natural disasters (flood, mudslide, avalanche) are among inclusions

Title: Struck by other falling object— n.e.c.
Description: Struck by a falling object event that is known but does not fit descriptions of event codes 6431 to 6433. The object is free falling and not dropped by a person, not falling from running equipment and not a tipping over.
Notes: Falling tree/branch is one inclusion among many

Title: In-flight crash, collision into structure, object, ground— n.e.c.
Description: Aircraft crashes in which the event is known but does not fit descriptions of event codes 2130 to 2133.
Notes: Includes bird strike; also covers crashes into terrain/trees

Title: Collision between rail vehicle and object(s)— n.e.c.
Description: Injuries resulting from collisions between rail vehicles and objects or animals, except other rail vehicles or roadway vehicles.
Notes: Includes train striking animal or fallen tree

Title: Collision with moving object or animal in roadway
Description: Moving vehicles that strike or are struck by moving objects or animals in a public roadway.
Notes: Animal collision on roadway; wildlife only if animal is wild

Title: Collision with object or animal on side of roadway
Description: Moving vehicles that strike objects or animals on the side or shoulder of a public roadway, outside of the lanes of travel.
Notes: Animal collision beside roadway; wildlife only if animal is wild

Title: Nonroadway collision with object or animal in path of travel— unspecified
Description: Nonroadway collisions with objects other than motorized land vehicles and mobile equipment when information about how the objects came into contact with the vehicle, specified in codes 2721 to 2729, is unknown.
Notes: Includes object OR animal; wildlife only if animal is wild

Title: Collision with moving object or animal, nonroadway
Description: Moving vehicles or mobile equipment that strike or are struck by moving objects or animals while driving, operating in nonroadway areas.
Notes: Includes object OR animal; wildlife only if animal is wild

Title: Nonroadway collision with object or animal — n.e.c.
Description: Moving vehicles that strike objects where the incident occurred on a private roadway or nonroadway area that are not described in codes 2721 through 2723.
Notes: Includes object OR animal; wildlife only if animal is wild

Title: Contact with animals

Title: Contact with animals— unspecified

Title: Bitten or stung by animal

Title: Bitten or stung by animal— unspecified
Description: Injuries resulting from being bitten or stung by an animal when a more specific code from 6211 to 6213 cannot be determined

Title: Bite or sting— insects, "bugs"
Description: Bites and stings from all types of "bugs". That is insects, arachnids, and myriapods (e.g. centipedes). Use this code regardless of whether the creature is considered venomous or not and whether or not the bite transmitted an illness, such as Lyme disease, West Nile virus, etc.

Title: Venomous animal bite— except "bugs"
Description: Venomous animal bite or contact, excluding bites and stings from bugs.

Title: Non-venomous animal bites— except "bugs"
Description: Injuries resulting from being bitten by a non- venomous animal

Title: Struck by animal
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Struck by animal— unspecified
Description: Contact with a non-venomous animal, except bites, when a more specific event code from 6221 to 6229 cannot be determined.

Title: Gored, rammed by animal
Description: Contact with a charging or butting animal with or without puncture by a horn.

Title: Stepped on, kicked, trampled by animal
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Mauled, clawed, scratched by animal
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Struck by animal— n.e.c.
Description: Contact with animal that does not fit descriptions of codes 6220-6223

Title: Multiple types of contact with animals
Description: Combination of one of more contact codes from 620 to 6229.

Title: Contact with animals— n.e.c.
Description: Contact with animals when a more specific event code that is known but does not fit descriptions of event codes from 621 to 628.

Title: Dirt, earth, mud
Description: Wet or dry dirt and earth that may be found in nature or used as a building material.
Notes: Soil saturation / mud proxy; not strictly environmental-condition code

Description: This major group classifies plants, trees, and vegetation in a natural or unprocessed condition. Source group 546, trees, logs, limbs, includes cut trees with or without limbs as well as tree branches. Thorns are coded according to the relevant plant.

Title: Plants, trees, vegetation— unspecified
Description: Plants in unprocessed state when a mores specific code from 5411 through 549 cannot be determined.

Title: Organic dusts
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Pollen
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Grain dust
Description: Dust from grain

Title: Organic dust— n.e.c.
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Description: Harvested grain that has been processed.

Title: Field crops
Description: Unharvested crops still in the field and harvested but unprocessed crops.

Title: Poison ivy, oak, sumac, rhus
Description: This code is for creeping vine plants that have irritative properties.

Title: Brush, shrubs, undergrowth
Description: Smaller woody plants used for landscaping or occurring in forest undergrowth.

Title: Trees, logs, limbs
Description: Trees and their various components which have not been processed into intermediate goods.

Description: Parts of trees that are known but do not match descriptions of codes 5461 through 5464.

Description: Plant materials that are in an advanced state of decomposition.

Title: Other plants, vegetation
Description: Other plants in an unprocessed state where details are known but do not match descriptions of codes 540 through 547.

Title: Bodies of water
Description: Part of the earth's surface that is naturally covered with water.

Title: Bodies of water— unspecified
Description: Bodies of water with too little information to choose a code from 671 through 679.

Title: Ponds, lakes
Description: Ponds and lakes that either occur naturally or were created due to damming a water source or digging

Title: Rivers, streams
Description: Natural body of water that flows across the earth.

Title: Coastal waters
Description: Coastal bodies of deep salt and brackish water

Title: Oceans, seas
Description: Large natural body of salt water.

Title: Bodies of water— n.e.c.
Description: Natural water body that is known but does not match codes 670 through 674. Includes shallow wetland areas.

Title: Environmental and elemental conditions
Description: This major group classifies conditions of the environment such as air pressure, temperature, and other atmospheric conditions, as well as events such as natural disasters. Select weather and atmospheric conditions or geological events (floods, earthquakes, avalanches) as the source of injury when that is the only possible source identified.

Title: Environmental and elemental conditions— unspecified
Description: Environmental and elemental conditions where a more specific code from 9510 to 9599 cannot be determined.

Title: Disasters— except weather
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Disasters— except weather, unspecified
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Avalanche, mudslide, rockslide
Description: Avalanche or other slide involving earth, ground, or rocks.

Title: Earthquake
Description: Earthquake or aftershock of earthquakes

Title: Wildfire
Description: Uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation

Title: Flooding— except weather related
Description: Displacement of a large volume of water, generally from an ocean or a large lake.

Title: Disasters— except weather, n.e.c.
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Weather, atmospheric conditions
Description: This Source Group classifies weather and atmospheric conditions. If rain or high winds are a result of a hurricane or tornado, code the hurricane or tornado as the source. When the injury results from a weather condition, but is inflicted by another specific source, code the specific source. For example, if high winds result in blowing sawdust which irritates the employee’s eyes, the sawdust should be coded as the source.

Title: Weather, atmospheric conditions— unspecified
Description: Weather and atmospheric conditions where a more specific code from 9521 to 9529 cannot be determined.

Title: Ice, sleet, snow, hail
Description: Frozen precipitation generated outside of a storm.

Title: Tornado, hurricane, typhoon
Description: Storm or atmospheric condition that typical has strong winds and/or precipitation.

Title: Rain
Description: Liquid precipitation generated outside of a storm.

Title: Fog, mist, haze
Description: Fog, mist, haze the occurs naturally as part of the weather and environment.

Title: High winds, gusts, turbulence
Description: Winds, gusts, turbulence that occur outside of a storm.

Title: Lightning
Description: Lightning that originates in the atmosphere.

Title: Waves, surges, rough seas
Description: Waves and other rough seas that affect the worker or maritime vessel.

Title: Multiple weather and atmospheric conditions
Description: (No separate definition in manual; see title)

Title: Weather, atmospheric conditions— n.e.c.
Description: Weather and atmospheric conditions that do not match descriptions of codes 9521 through 9528.

Title: Environmental and elemental pressure
Description: This Source Group classifies abnormal environmental air pressure conditions as well as pressurized air. Low pressure refers to rarefied air at extreme elevations.

Title: Environmental pressure— unspecified
Description: Air pressure where a more specific code from 9531 to 9539 cannot be determined.

Title: Atmospheric pressure—high or low
Description: The effects of altitude and being underground (but not underwater).

Title: Water pressure—high or low
Description: Effects or low or high water pressure that might lead to decompression sickness.

Title: Pressurized air—blast
Description: Blasts of air, typically for a device designed for that purpose like a blower or sand blaster.

Title: Pressurized water—blast
Description: A pressurized blast of water typically from an instrument designed for that purpose like a hose or pressure washer.

Title: Oxygen deficient environment
Description: Environments, typically associated with confined spaces, where oxygen has been displaced by other gases, resulting in asphyxiation.

Title: Environmental pressure— n.e.c.
Description: Air pressure that does not match descriptions of codes 9531 through 9535.

Title: Temperature extremes—environmental
Description: This Source Group classifies atmospheric and environmental temperature extremes—either indoors or outdoors. Codes in this category are used primarily in instances of heat stroke, heat exhaustion, hypothermia, etc.

Title: Temperature extremes—environmental— unspecified
Description: Temperature extremes - environment where a more specific code from 9541 to 9542 cannot be determined.

Title: Cold—environmental
Description: Cold from the environment like from frigid outdoor temperatures or in an indoor food locker.

Title: Heat—environmental
Description: Heat from high outdoor temperatures or from a hot indoor area like proximate to a blast furnace.

Title: Light, radiation, noise
Description: This source includes the energy waves that compose natural and artificial light, noise, and radiation. Note that, with the exception of code 9551, Sun, this Source Group refers to the energy waves themselves and not to the items that produce them.

Title: Light, radiation, noise— unspecified
Description: Light, radiation, and noise where a more specific code from 9551 to 9559 cannot be determined.

Title: Sun
Description: Light and glare generated by the sun that affects the worker's vision.

Title: Fire, flame
Description: Fire, flame, and other hot parts of combustion.

Title: Welders’ flash
Description: Flash from the process of welding.

Title: Lasers
Description: Intense beams of light (or other electromagnetic radiation) created by stimulating emission of photons from excited atoms or molecules.

Title: Other ultraviolet (UV) light
Description: This code is used for ultraviolet electromagnetic radiation (with wavelength from 10 nm to 400 nm).

Title: Particle Radiation
Description: This code is used for radiation of energy by means of fast-moving subatomic particles.

Title: Noise
Description: Noise and other sound on the audible spectrum.

Title: Light, radiation, noise— n.e.c.
Description: Light, radiation, and noise that do not match descriptions of codes 9551 through 9557.

Title: Other environmental and elemental conditions
Description: This Source Group includes other environmental conditions that have not been covered in a previous category.

Title: Effects of electric current
